description: Deterministic A4V3 translator-lint checks for recurring manual DZ mistakes: dead declarations, self-referential deontic scope, completed-event obligation names, double-coded deontic norms, temporal relation smells in deontic files, vacuous responsibility implications, label-only universal constraints, fact-like universal constraints, opaque numeric sorts, weak based-on links, and shared semantic tokens that live only in predicate names.

rules.name: unused_rel_fun_declaration_count
rules.what_it_counts: local rel/fun declarations that are never referenced by assertion bodies, deontic fields, or another declaration signature.
rules.how_to_compute: Parse top-level A4V3 declarations, collect declared names and all references from fact/constraint/axiom bodies plus deontic fields and signatures; count unused rel/fun declarations.
rules.bad_value_means: The IR likely contains stale helper relations/functions left behind after a refactor.
rules.repair_target: Delete the declaration or restore the formula body that uses it.

rules.name: unused_sort_entity_declaration_count
rules.what_it_counts: local sort/entity/val declarations that are not referenced by assertion bodies, deontic fields, or signatures.
rules.how_to_compute: Same declaration-use graph as unused_rel_fun_declaration_count, but for sort/entity/val declarations.
rules.bad_value_means: The IR may contain support ontology that no current formula uses.
rules.repair_target: Inspect whether the declaration is intentionally supporting context; otherwise delete it.

rules.name: self_referential_deontic_scope_count
rules.what_it_counts: obligation/permission/prohibition declarations where scope equals one of the declaration parameter sorts.
rules.how_to_compute: For each deontic declaration, parse parameter sorts and compare them to the optional scope field.
rules.bad_value_means: The deontic scope repeats the argument type and adds no contextual semantics.
rules.repair_target: Remove scope or replace it with a real contextual sort such as approval, cessation, deadline, or policy context.

rules.name: past_participle_obligation_name_count
rules.what_it_counts: obligation names whose first token looks like a past participle rather than an action verb.
rules.how_to_compute: Tokenize the obligation name and flag the first token if it ends with -ed/-en or is an irregular completed-event form such as made/taken/done.
rules.bad_value_means: The obligation reads like an already-completed event rather than a norm requiring an action.
rules.repair_target: Rename to an action-style verb form, e.g. submit_... rather than submitted_....

rules.name: double_coded_deontic_norm_count
rules.what_it_counts: possible cases where one norm is encoded both as a deontic declaration and as a hard constraint over the same action/target.
rules.how_to_compute: For each obligation/prohibition action+target, search constraints whose body/name contains an action root or nominalization and the same target.
rules.bad_value_means: The same normative requirement may be represented as both violable obligation and logically mandatory constraint.
rules.repair_target: Choose either a deontic declaration or a hard constraint, unless the two formulas intentionally express distinct claims.

rules.name: temporal_rel_in_deontic_context_count
rules.what_it_counts: declared temporal-looking relations such as prior_to/before/after that are used in assertion bodies while the file also contains deontic declarations.
rules.how_to_compute: If the entry has obligation/permission/prohibition, scan used rel names for temporal tokens.
rules.bad_value_means: A deontic/temporal requirement may have been modeled as an ad-hoc ordinary relation.
rules.repair_target: Inspect whether the relation should be represented by deontic scope/deadline or a first-class temporal construct.

rules.name: vacuous_responsibility_implication_count
rules.what_it_counts: responsibility constraints of the form rel(decision,item) implies responsible_for(actor,decision) under only universal quantifiers.
rules.how_to_compute: Detect forall/forall implication patterns where responsible_for is guarded by the existence of a decision relation and no existential decision is introduced.
rules.bad_value_means: The formula can be true when no decision exists; this may be too weak if the source requires a decision for each governed item.
rules.repair_target: If source warrants it, rewrite to forall item, exists decision: decision_regarding(decision,item) and responsible_for(actor,decision).

rules.name: bare_universal_predicate_constraint_count
rules.what_it_counts: constraints whose entire body is forall variables, P(variables), with no equality, comparison, implication, aggregate, or value link.
rules.how_to_compute: Parse each constraint body after comments/whitespace normalization and match the exact pattern of one or more forall binders followed by a single predicate call.
rules.bad_value_means: The IR may be hiding semantic content in a predicate name while the formula body only asserts a label universally.
rules.repair_target: Replace the label-only predicate with a formula that links the relevant values, or document it as an intentionally weak marker.

rules.name: fact_like_universal_constraint_count
rules.what_it_counts: constraints whose body is universal quantifiers followed by descriptive/procedural atom(s), with no equality, comparison, implication, existential witness, aggregate, or temporal operator.
rules.how_to_compute: Normalize each constraint body, strip leading forall binders, and flag the remaining formula if it is only one or more positive atom calls joined by and.
rules.bad_value_means: The declaration may be a descriptive source fact written as a hard constraint.
rules.repair_target: Use fact for descriptive/procedural assertions, or add explicit limiting structure if the source really gives a hard constraint.

rules.name: numeric_operation_on_non_numeric_sort_count
rules.what_it_counts: function calls used in numeric comparisons or sum aggregates where the declared function return sort is not a known numeric/value sort.
rules.how_to_compute: Collect fun return sorts, then scan claim bodies for function calls in <=/>=/</> numeric-literal comparisons or as the value term of sum(...).
rules.bad_value_means: The IR uses an opaque/entity sort as if it were a numeric value.
rules.repair_target: Change the function return sort to a numeric/value sort such as Percent, or add an explicit value-extraction function and use that in arithmetic.

rules.name: basis_relation_without_value_link_count
rules.what_it_counts: constraints whose name says X based_on Y, but whose body does not mention both an X-like dependent value term and a Y-like basis value term.
rules.how_to_compute: Tokenize constraint names around based_on/basis, ignore generic tokens, then compare dependent/basis token groups against non-marker function/predicate calls in the body.
rules.bad_value_means: A source dependency may be represented only by a name, not by formula terms that connect the dependent value to its basis.
rules.repair_target: Mention both the dependent value and the basis value in the formula body, or document the relation as an intentionally weak provenance marker.

rules.name: shared_name_token_without_structural_carrier_count
rules.what_it_counts: claim blocks where the same non-generic semantic token appears in two or more relation/function names but has no structural carrier.
rules.how_to_compute: For each fact/constraint/axiom/prop/theorem body, collect declared rel/fun calls, tokenize their names, ignore generic tokens, and flag repeated tokens that are not represented by a sort/entity/val, relation/function signature sort, or formula-body argument.
rules.bad_value_means: A semantic link may be encoded only by repeated words inside predicate names, rather than by an explicit shared entity/sort/argument in formula structure.
rules.repair_target: Introduce a structural carrier for the repeated concept, e.g. a sort/entity and relation arguments, or document why the repeated token is intentionally only lexical.
